A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEGA and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Inspection of both complete documents supports reliable matching despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MEGA rendering-quality, speed, storage, and component-ablation results on Technicolor and Neural 3D Video, including scene-level appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and reports additional network-size, loss-weight, opacity-loss, and view-input experiments in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix B retain the DC–AC color representation, temporal-viewpoint deformation, opacity regularization, pruning, and FP16/zip compression. The added experimental variants do not revise the proposed full method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five Technicolor and six Neural 3D Video scenes for dynamic novel-view synthesis. New ablations use the existing Fabien and Birthday scenes. Noise, ultra-fast motion, and view extrapolation are discussed as limitations without added evaluations of those conditions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged. New Table 6 compares MEGA with 4DGS, STG, and E-D3DGS with and without the opacity loss, adding targeted regularized-baseline variants to the comparison evidence.

E3.justification: Existing splits, resolutions, metrics, and 30k-iteration training settings are retained. Appendix C adds controlled settings involving larger color/deformation MLPs, alternative loss weights, opacity regularization on baselines, and removal of view-direction input.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially broadens the original component ablations with four distinct investigations: network capacity, loss-weight sensitivity, transfer of opacity regularization to other methods, and the contribution of view-direction input. Tables 6–7 provide new evidence for these questions; the earlier ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added appendix experiments continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Tables 6–7 add targeted ablation results: for example, the Birthday view-input experiment reports 32.02 dB and 0.91M Gaussians for full MEGA versus 27.35 dB and 1.54M without view input. These are newly reported variant results, not improvements to retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, temporal-slicing formulation, and Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical content. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; the added mechanism discussion is qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same method claims and approximately 190×/125× storage reductions with comparable rendering quality and speed. The new appendix evidence supports existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds explanations for lightweight MLP sufficiency, possible conflicts between opacity sparsity and baseline motion models, and the importance of view conditioning. New Appendix D identifies specific limitations involving motion blur, color inconsistency, ultra-fast motion, and extrapolation beyond training views, with suggested remedies.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract and documents loss-weight settings for the new sweeps. Existing implementation and default-network details remain. The enlarged-network variants are labelled 'Large' without corresponding layer-size specifications.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands references on Gaussian representation efficiency and applications, including MVSplat, Scaffold-GS, GaussianEditor, and Feature 3DGS. Appendix D introduces Robust Gaussian Splatting as a possible future remedy. The central positioning within 4DGS compression remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering are retained, with localized wording edits, updated affiliations/contact information, and acknowledgments. The supplement gains distinct ablation and limitations sections without a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Figure 1's panels become vertically arranged; Painter moves from Figure 5 into Figure 7, and the former Figure 7 becomes Figure 6. Existing qualitative comparisons are retained, and Tables 6–7 are added.

improvement.justification: Appendix C strengthens evidence for design choices, Appendix D makes applicability limits explicit, and the code-access statement improves reproducibility information. These are useful gains around an unchanged method and unchanged benchmark results. Their significance is limited by the new tests covering only two existing scenes and the enlarged-network configurations remaining underspecified.
